items.subject: Petition under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for adoption of tariff for the 50 MW and 350 MW Solar Power Plants connected to the Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) linked with setting-up of solar manufacturing plant, selected through competitive bidding process as per the Guidelines dated 03.08.2017 of the Central Government as amended from time to time and interpreted and modified by the Central Government vide subsequent communications. Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited

Submission of the Petitioner:
7. The Petitioner has submitted that on 25.6.2019, it issued a Request for Selection (RfS)
along with Standard Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and Power Sale Agreement (PSA)
documents for the ‘Selection of Solar Power Developers for Setting-up of 7 GW ISTS
Connected Solar PV Power Plants linked with Setting up of 2 GW (Per Annum) Solar
Manufacturing Plant under Global Competitive Bidding’ as per the Guidelines dated
3.8.2017 on the ISN Electronic Tender System (ETS) e-bidding portal. As per the
Petitioner, the entire tender was split into two Bidding Packages (1) Package A: For setting
up the Solar Manufacturing Plants related to Cells (500 MW) and Modules (500 MW); and
(2) Package B: For setting up the Solar Manufacturing Plants related to Ingots (500 MW)
and Wafers (500 MW). Two Blocks were to be allocated under each of the above two
packages. The successful bidder was assured of the PPA up to 2000 MW against 500 MW
of a Solar Manufacturing Plant under Bidding Package A and up to 1500 MW against 500
MW of manufacturing capacity under Package B. Thus, the aggregated Solar PV Power
Plant capacity stipulated under the above arrangement was a maximum of 7000 MW for
the aggregated manufacturing capacity of 2000 MW (1000 MW under Package A and 1000
MW under Package B). In response to the RfS, three bids were received offering an
aggregate capacity of 8000 MW under Package A. However, no response was received
under Package B. All three bids under Package A were found to fully meet the technical
criteria and qualified for opening the financial bid. As per the eligibility criteria mentioned
in the RfS, all three bidders were shortlisted for participating in the e-reverse auction under
Package A. The e-reverse auction was conducted on 22.11.2019 on the ISN ETS e-bidding
portal, and pursuant thereto, two bidders, namely, Azure Power Private India (in short
“Azure Power”) and Adani Green Energy Four Limited (in short “Adani Green”) were
allocated 2000 MW each at a tariff of Rs.2.92/kWh.
8. Thereafter, in terms of Amendment-VI to RfS, the under-subscribed capacity under
Bidding Package-B, i.e., up to 3000 MW of the Solar PV Power Plant linked with 1000
MW of the Solar Manufacturing Plant, was transferred to Bidding Package A. The ratio of
the Solar Manufacturing Plant to the Solar Power Plant was kept at 1:4 in terms of the
provisions of RfS. Post transfer of capacity, the total tendered capacity under Bidding
Package-A became 8000 MW of Solar PV Power Plant linked with 2000 MW of Solar

Hearing dated 12.05.2026:
17. The Petitioner reiterated its submissions in the present Petition and submitted that out of
the total awarded capacity of 12 GW under the RfS, the Commission adopted the tariff for
aggregate capacity of 8900 MW Solar Power Projects (1900 MW under Package I and
7000 MW under Packages II to IV), for which the PPAs and PSAs were already executed,
vide order dated 02.04.2022 in Petition No. 286/AT/2021. Thereafter, the Commission,
vide order dated 05.11.2023 in Petition No.224/AT/2023, adopted the tariff for another
334 MW Solar Power Projects (Package I) as tied up by the Petitioner, and for the
remaining capacity, the Petitioner was granted liberty to approach the Commission once
such capacity is tied up under the PPAs and PSAs. Pursuant thereto, the Petitioner has
further tied up another 400 MW of the remaining capacity and is, accordingly, seeking
adoption of a tariff for such capacity. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner,
the Commission directed that the petition be admitted and notice be issued to the
Respondents.
Hearing dated 11.06.2026
18. The Petitioner informed, during the hearing, of subsequent developments in the matter,
that the Petitioner is soon expected to sign a PSA with PSPCL for 250 MW once the
PSERC approves such procurement, for which the order has already been reserved.
Accordingly, counsel sought liberty to bring on record these subsequent developments,
along with the signed PPA and PSA for another 250 MW, by way of an additional affidavit.
However, in response to a specific query of the Commission regarding the prayer for
adoption of the tariff in the present Petition being limited only to 400 MW, bringing on
record any subsequent PPA and PSAs may require a formal amendment and may also
protract the present proceedings, the counsel for the Petitioner did not pursue her request
to bring on record the subsequent developments. Considering the submissions made by the
counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission reserved the matter for order.
Analysis and Decision:
19. The Commission has considered the submissions of the Petitioner and perused the
documents placed on record. The Commission now proceeds to consider the prayer of the
Petitioner as regards the petition under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for adoption
